findings.body: The response and profile template still expose the website host and, for matching domains, its path through `website_name`, bypassing the deliberate restriction on untrusted profile fields.
findings.failure_mode: Field-level access control removes the source attribute while leaving equivalent derived information in serialized output.
findings.impact: The response and profile template still expose the website host and, for matching domains, its path through `website_name`, bypassing the deliberate restriction on untrusted profile fields.
findings.root_cause: The new attribute is derived from the restricted `website` field but was registered as an unrestricted serializer attribute.
findings.suggested_fix: Apply the same restriction to `website_name`, either by adding it to `untrusted_attributes` and removing the custom inclusion method, or by implementing `include_website_name?` with the `scope.restrict_user_fields?(object)` guard. Add a serializer test with a populated TL0 website.
findings.title: Derived website field bypasses restricted-profile filtering
findings.trigger: An anonymous visitor requests a trust-level-0 user's profile after that user has populated the website field, causing `scope.restrict_user_fields?(object)` to suppress the original `website` attribute.
findings.verifier_reason: Line 43 adds `:website_name` to attributes. The `untrusted_attributes` list (lines 105-111) includes `:website` but not `:website_name`. The `include_website_name` method (line 153) only checks `website.present?` without the `scope.restrict_user_fields?(object)` guard used by untrusted_attributes. This allows `website_name` to be serialized for TL0 users viewed anonymously, bypassing the restriction applied to `website`.

findings.body: ActiveModel Serializers does not recognize this as the `include_website_name?` callback, so the newly added API key is emitted unconditionally, typically as `website_name: null`, instead of being omitted as the method intends.
findings.failure_mode: The dead inclusion method is never consulted, changing the response shape for profiles that have no displayable website name.
findings.impact: ActiveModel Serializers does not recognize this as the `include_website_name?` callback, so the newly added API key is emitted unconditionally, typically as `website_name: null`, instead of being omitted as the method intends.
findings.root_cause: The callback name omits the trailing `?` required by the serializer convention used throughout this class.
findings.suggested_fix: Rename the callback to `include_website_name?` and make it both presence- and visibility-aware, or remove it and let `untrusted_attributes :website_name` generate the correctly named callback.
findings.title: Serializer inclusion callback is missing its predicate suffix
findings.trigger: Any user without a website is serialized through `UserSerializer`.
findings.verifier_reason: Line 153 shows `def include_website_name` without trailing `?`. ActiveModel::Serializers 0.8.x (per Gemfile) uses `include_<attr>?` convention as seen throughout the file (e.g., `include_card_image_badge_id?` at line 161). Without the `?`, the method won't be called as an inclusion predicate, so `website_name` will always be serialized when present.

raw_findings.body: Although DNS hostnames are case-insensitive, the serializer treats the hosts as different and displays only `Example.com`, omitting the path that this change is intended to show.
raw_findings.failure_mode: Equivalent DNS names take the external-domain branch and produce an incomplete website label.
raw_findings.impact: Although DNS hostnames are case-insensitive, the serializer treats the hosts as different and displays only `Example.com`, omitting the path that this change is intended to show.
raw_findings.root_cause: Raw hostname strings are compared with case-sensitive Ruby equality and suffix operations.
raw_findings.suggested_fix: Normalize both parsed hosts to lowercase for all comparisons while preserving the desired original or canonical casing for display, and add a mixed-case hostname test.
raw_findings.title: Hostname matching is incorrectly case-sensitive
raw_findings.trigger: A user stores a same-site URL such as `http://Example.com/user` while `Discourse.current_hostname` is `example.com`.

raw_findings.body: The relationship check only recognizes the instance as a subdomain of the website, not the reverse, so this common same-domain URL is displayed as `www.example.com` without `/user`.
raw_findings.failure_mode: A valid same-domain URL is misclassified as external depending solely on which host is the subdomain.
raw_findings.impact: The relationship check only recognizes the instance as a subdomain of the website, not the reverse, so this common same-domain URL is displayed as `www.example.com` without `/user`.
raw_findings.root_cause: The fallback suffix comparison is asymmetric and checks only whether `website_host` is a parent of `discourse_host`.
raw_findings.suggested_fix: Use a symmetric, dot-boundary-aware domain relationship check, or compare normalized registrable domains, and cover the apex-instance/subdomain-website direction in the serializer spec.
raw_findings.title: Same-domain detection fails when the website is a subdomain of the instance
raw_findings.trigger: The instance runs at an apex host such as `example.com` and a profile website is `http://www.example.com/user`.

raw_findings.body: Both hosts reduce to `github.io`, so the serializer incorrectly classifies unrelated domains as the same domain and displays the website's path.
raw_findings.failure_mode: Unrelated hosts with the same public suffix enter the same-domain display branch.
raw_findings.impact: Both hosts reduce to `github.io`, so the serializer incorrectly classifies unrelated domains as the same domain and displays the website's path.
raw_findings.root_cause: The sibling-host heuristic treats every last-two-or-more-label suffix as an organizational domain without accounting for public suffixes.
raw_findings.suggested_fix: Compare canonical registrable domains using a public-suffix-aware implementation, with explicit handling for IP literals, instead of assuming all labels after the first identify common ownership.
raw_findings.title: Dropping the first label conflates unrelated public-suffix tenants
raw_findings.trigger: The instance and website are separate tenants under a multi-label public suffix, for example `forum.github.io` and `attacker.github.io/account`.

raw_findings.body: The previous client-side extraction displayed `example.com:3000`, but `URI#host` returns only `example.com`; the new label therefore hides the port and can misrepresent which service the link targets.
raw_findings.failure_mode: Serialization silently loses part of the URL authority when producing `website_name`.
raw_findings.impact: The previous client-side extraction displayed `example.com:3000`, but `URI#host` returns only `example.com`; the new label therefore hides the port and can misrepresent which service the link targets.
raw_findings.root_cause: The same `URI#host` value is used for both domain comparison and user-visible authority text even though it excludes the port.
raw_findings.suggested_fix: Keep a host-only value for domain comparisons and construct a separate display authority that appends an explicitly specified non-default port. Add a serializer test for a port-bearing URL.
raw_findings.title: Parsed host drops non-default website ports from the display name
raw_findings.trigger: A profile contains a URL with an explicit non-default port, such as `http://example.com:3000/user`.
